summary.text: Chellie Pingree is the Democratic U.S. Representative for Maine's 1st District, which she has represented since 2009, and won re-election on November 3, 2026.

Before Congress she ran a farm and a knitwear business on North Haven, served in the Maine Senate (including as majority leader), and led Common Cause. She sits on the House Appropriations and Agriculture committees.

paragraphs.text: Pingree was born on April 2, 1955, in Minneapolis, Minnesota, the youngest of four children, and moved to Maine as a teenager.
She attended the University of Southern Maine and earned a B.A. from the College of the Atlantic in 1979.

Pingree moved to North Haven, Maine, where she and her husband ran a small farm. In 1981 she started North Island Yarn (later North Island Designs), a knitting-kit business she sold in 1993, and she also served on the school board and as town tax assessor.

She served in the Maine Senate from 1992 to 2000, representing Knox County, and her peers elected her Senate majority leader in 1996. In her last session she sponsored the MaineRx prescription drug pricing bill.
Pingree ran unsuccessfully against U.S. Sen. Susan Collins in 2002 and then served as national president and CEO of Common Cause from 2003 to 2007.

She was elected to the U.S. House in 2008, the first woman elected to Congress from Maine's 1st District. She previously served on the Rules and Armed Services committees and currently sits on the Appropriations and Agriculture committees.

Pingree received a 2017 James Beard Leadership Award for her work on food system reform, and her office says provisions of her agriculture legislation were included in the 2014 and 2018 Farm Bills. She co-owns Nebo Lodge, a bed and breakfast and restaurant on North Haven started in 2006.
She won the November 3, 2026 general election with 65.9% of the vote to Ronald Russell's 34.1%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
